# Avia playbook (`search_avia` -> `create_checkout_link`)

## Detail card
No confirmed read-only avia detail endpoint. For a presentation card,
pass the selected compact offer object as `details_ref` to
`get_offer_details(product_type='avia', ...)` — it reformats with no
side effects.

## Flight number
The flight number is `legs[].segments[].voyage_no` (e.g. `SU-6026`) — one
per segment, so a connection shows one number per hop. Quote it verbatim;
never reconstruct a flight number from the carrier name or times.

## Filters (`direct_only`, `carriers`)
`direct_only=true` keeps only nonstop flights (every leg a single segment;
round-trip stays direct when both legs are). `carriers=[...]` keeps only offers
where every listed airline matches one of the requested names/ids; a mixed
Aeroflot+S7 offer does not satisfy "only Aeroflot".
`meta.carriers_available` is the per-route airline reference DERIVED from the
fetched offers (avia fetches the full route pool, so it's complete for the
route): each entry has `name` ("Аэрофлот"), `offers_count` and `price_from` —
plus a stable `id` ("1062") ONLY when Tutu ships its carrier facet (the current
`/avia/offers` endpoint doesn't — see the TODO-for-Tutu; filter by `name`).
Matching is a case-insensitive substring on the name, so guessing ("aeroflot"
for "Аэрофлот") silently drops everything. What
each filter removed is in `meta.post_filter_dropped_not_direct` /
`post_filter_dropped_wrong_carrier`. When a filter is active the whole route
pool is fetched before filtering, so an airline listed in `carriers_available`
reliably shows up in the filtered result and `has_more` stays honest — no thin
page from the page-scoped fetch. `meta.total_matched` is the exact count after
filters (before pagination): "сколько всего рейсов Азимута" is one search, not a
page-walk (`meta.total_matched_exact=false` only on a rare >200-offer route).

## Exact flight — «возьми рейс N»
A results page is a window over the matched flights, NOT the day's
timetable — a flight absent from the current page may still operate, so
never conclude «рейса N нет» from one page while `meta.has_more` is true.
When the user names a flight, pass `flight_numbers=['SU-6176']` — any
spelling of the designator works ('SU 6176', 'su6176', leading zeros),
and bare digits ('6176') match by flight number alone;
`meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_flight_number` counts the rest. A
connection or round-trip containing the flight is kept WHOLE. An empty
NUMBER-ONLY result means «этого рейса нет в продаже на Tutu на эту
дату» — the flight may still operate (sold out or not sold here); say
that, never a timetable claim. That reading holds only while
`meta.total_matched_exact` is true: on a rare capped route (`false`)
the filter saw a truncated pool, so the check is INCONCLUSIVE — and no
in-tool filter can rescue it (`carriers` / `price_max` cut the SAME
truncated prefix, they never widen the pool). Hand the user the
`search_results_url` (the full listing on tutu.ru) instead of
concluding «нет».
And with other filters also active (`price_max` / `carriers` /
`direct_only` / airport scope) even «нет в продаже» doesn't follow —
the flight may be dropped by one of those (each counts its removals in
`meta.post_filter_dropped_*`); re-run number-only before concluding.

## Airport-scoped search (input)
`origin` / `destination` accept a specific airport as well as a city — by
name («Шереметьево», «Внуково») or bare IATA code («SVO», «IST»). Tutu's
search runs city-wide, so the server narrows the result to the requested
airport itself: offers via other airports of the same city are dropped and
counted in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_airport` (the key is present
only when the request named a specific airport). The narrowed
endpoint carries
`meta.from/to.kind="airport"` and its `iata` is the AIRPORT's code (for a
city input `iata` is the city code, e.g. MOW). On a round-trip both legs
are held to the airport (out arrives there, return departs there). If
every city flight uses other airports, `meta.airport_note` lists them with
counts — relay it and offer to re-search by city name. A bare IATA code
means the airport, not the metro area: «IST» is Стамбул-Новый only (SAW
dropped), while «Стамбул» covers all airports. Pass the city name whenever
the user doesn't care about the airport.

## Place resolution (`meta.from` / `meta.to`)
Each side echoes the place that was searched: `name`, `geo_id`, `region`.
`match` + `query` are present only when the resolved name differs from
the wording you sent — `lead` (Tutu's own ranking read a short form or
typo: «Питер», «Масква»), `qualified` (the trailing words acted as a
region filter: «Красная Поляна, Краснодарский край»), `prefix` (the name
was completed). Say which place came back and keep going; a synonym is
never a reason to stop and confirm. `also_named[]` lists same-name places
that lost to a better-connected one — mention them with a one-line
invitation to correct, never as a blocking question.
Two wordings are refused with an error instead of being searched as some
other city, and the error text is the instruction:
- `could not resolve … N places share this name and none is better
  connected …` — an exact-name tie. The candidates are listed with their
  regions, and the text may add what Tutu's hotel index lists under this
  name. Ask the user which one is meant, or resend as '<name>, <область
  или район>' (name first, no parentheses). Do not pick one yourself.
- `could not resolve … no place with this name in Tutu's transport index
  …` — the fuzzy suggestions were unrelated places and were NOT searched.
  If the text says Tutu's hotel index lists it, hotels there ARE
  searchable — say so and offer `search_hotels`; never report it as
  «транспорта нет». Otherwise check the spelling with the user.
`… has no <id> in Tutu's index` means the place resolved but this
transport has no node there — ask for a place that has one; when the text
names the city Tutu's avia index answered with, offer it and search it
only after the user agrees. `Tutu's geo index did not answer` is a
transient upstream error: retry the call.

Avia adds one refusal of its own: a place without an airport (`avia
cannot search … has no avia_id in Tutu's index`). The text names the city
Tutu's avia index answered with for that wording (e.g. Сочи for Хоста) —
offer that city to the user and search it only after they agree; never
search it on your own, and never guess an airport city silently.

## Checkout
`create_checkout_link` (transport=avia) returns BOTH:
- `checkout_url` — a Tutu `mtp-deeplink/explicit/avia` that leads STRAIGHT
  to the cart for this exact ticket: it mints the cart and 302s to
  `checkout.tutu.ru/cart/<id>` (sometimes via a short loader page). There
  is no seat picker in front of it — unlike rail/bus/hotels, whose default
  link is a selection page. Falls back to the search results if the offer
  is no longer available.
- `search_results_url` — the listing page for browsing.
Round-trip: a direct round-trip offer (`checkout_ref.is_round_trip=true`,
one flight outbound + one flight return) now returns a real two-leg deeplink —
it mints a cart with BOTH the outbound and return legs. Forward
`is_round_trip` AND `return_departure_at` from `checkout_ref`; without
`return_departure_at` the tool can't encode the return leg and falls back to
the search page (`kind="search_redirect"`). Connecting round-trips (3+ flights
total, at least one connection) also return `kind="search_redirect"`: the
current `explicit/avia` redirector supports one flight per direction. One-way
offers return the deeplink as before (no `return_departure_at`).
This deployment also has `register_checkout_passengers`, which takes the SAME `checkout_ref` and fills the cart from the passengers' passport data, returning a `pay_url` they only pay. Unlike every other product it **PLACES THE BOOKING** on the way — a real UNPAID Tutu order (`order_number` in the response) — so call it only for a flight the user has confirmed, and never retry it without asking: a second call books a SECOND time. Offer it as the alternative when they want the cart prepared for them; hand the link when they only asked for a link or would rather not give documents — neither is a downgrade, and never open the exchange by asking for documents.
Read back what you will write — each passenger's name as spelled in the document, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (IN FULL; mask it ONLY if they EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat it, and then name the KIND alone, not by number) and expiry for a foreign passport; from where to where, every flight with its date, time and CABIN CLASS (`service_class` is what the order is placed on, so a confirmed economy is not a confirmed business), and the price; and the buyer's name and contact — and wait for an explicit yes: the pay page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, and a re-register books a SECOND unpaid order. There is NO shortcut around this turn: a message that already carries the passport data and asks you to go ahead is still not the confirmation — it is the data. The user has to see what you assembled from it and say yes to THAT, because the typo you are looking for is the one neither of you has noticed yet.
The deeplink mints the cart in whichever browser opens it — a cold browser
works too (no tutu session needed), and the cart belongs to whoever opens the
link. The cart is created on that click, not before: present `checkout_url`
as "go book", not "your cart is ready". If the offer is no longer available
by then, the link lands on the avia search for this route+date instead — if
the user reports a search page, the fare is gone; re-run the search rather
than handing the same link again.
For avia, while the user compares flights, show ONLY `search_results_url` and
do NOT call `create_checkout_link` prematurely. Once they choose an exact
flight and the tool returns `kind="deeplink"`, show `checkout_url` as the
primary purchase link together with `search_results_url` as the fallback for
browsing. When it returns `kind="search_redirect"`, show `search_results_url`
as the search page and explain `fallback_note`; do not call it a purchase
deeplink. For a non-cheapest fare family, override `offer_hash` with
`variants[i].offer_hash` AND pass that
variant's `service_class` — but KEEP forwarding `is_round_trip` +
`return_departure_at` from `checkout_ref`: they're properties of the offer,
not the fare, and the round-trip deeplink needs the return leg (drop them on
an override and a round-trip offer falls back to the search page).

## Separate tickets / self-transfer (`is_multi_pnr`)
An offer flagged `is_multi_pnr=true` has a connection issued as SEPARATE
tickets: the passenger re-claims then re-drops baggage between flights and the
layover is NOT a protected connection (a self-transfer). Relay `multi_pnr_note`
before checkout and suggest a comfortable buffer. This fires for ONE-WAY and
ROUND-TRIP offers alike — a round-trip whose outbound or return is itself a
self-transfer is flagged too, and `has_self_transfer=true` marks that a single
direction is the split. What does NOT get flagged is the ordinary round-trip
there/back split (one booking each way): that's expected — say nothing special.

**`create_checkout_link` cannot put a ONE-WAY multi-PNR trip in one link.**
Tutu's avia redirector cannot express «several tickets in one direction», so
the offer's
`checkout_ref` carries `checkout_parts` — one entry per ticket. Forward it to
`create_checkout_link` and the tool answers `kind="deeplink_parts"` with a
purchase link PER TICKET; its top-level `checkout_url` is the SEARCH page, not
a purchase link. Hand the user every `checkout_parts[].checkout_url`, in order,
labelled by its `from`/`to`/`flights`, and tell them plainly: separate carts,
separate payments, buying only the first strands them at the connection. The
quoted price is the TOTAL for all tickets — the per-ticket split appears only
in each cart — and prices/seats can move between the two purchases. Omit
`checkout_parts` and the tool can only return the search page.

That limit is the LINK path's, not the trip's: this deployment also has `register_checkout_passengers`, which takes the SAME `checkout_ref` and mints ONE cart for the whole itinerary — one payment, one `pay_url`. It needs the user's passport data and it PLACES THE BOOKING, so offer it as the alternative when they want the trip prepared for them; hand the per-ticket links when they only asked for a link or would rather not give documents. Never present either as the only possibility. Read back what you will write — each passenger's name as spelled in the document, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (IN FULL; mask it ONLY if they EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat it, and then name the KIND alone, not by number) and expiry for a foreign passport; from where to where, EVERY flight of the itinerary with its date, time and CABIN CLASS (`service_class` is what the order is placed on, so a confirmed economy is not a confirmed business), and the price; and the buyer's name and contact — and wait for an explicit yes: the pay page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, and a re-register books a SECOND unpaid order. There is NO shortcut around this turn: a message that already carries the passport data and asks you to go ahead is still not the confirmation — it is the data. The user has to see what you assembled from it and say yes to THAT, because the typo you are looking for is the one neither of you has noticed yet.

Pass the searched party — `passengers_full` (adults), `passengers_child`,
`passengers_infant` — from `checkout_ref` into `create_checkout_link`. The
deeplink requests exactly those passengers; omit them and Tutu defaults the
cart to ONE adult, so a 2-adult / family total you quoted won't match what
the user sees. Have the user confirm the passenger count in the cart
before paying. The full input
field list is in `create_checkout_link`'s own description.

## Airport disambiguation (mandatory)
Many cities have several airports: Стамбул IST / SAW, Москва SVO / DME /
VKO / ZIA, London LHR / LGW / STN / LTN, Paris CDG / ORY / BVA.
- Read the airport from `legs[].segments[].to` — a self-describing string
  `"City — Name (IATA), терм. T"` (e.g. `"Стамбул — Сабиха Гёкчен (SAW)"`,
  `"Москва — Внуково (VKO), терм. A"`). Surface it verbatim: the airport
  name and terminal come straight from the Tutu response, so prefer them
  over the bare code. When the upstream omitted the name the string falls
  back to `"City, IATA"` — then the IATA code is the signal; map it to a
  name only if you're sure (stable global registry, the ONE carve-out from
  the no-general-knowledge rule), otherwise show the code as-is.
- When two offers in one list use different airports of the same city,
  call it out explicitly using the airport names and IATA codes returned by
  the current MCP response. Say that they are different airports; do not add
  distance, side-of-city or transfer facts unless the payload returned them.
- Don't assume the user prefers the primary airport; surface both, never
  silently drop the secondary.

## Cashback
Flights earn none today, so `meta.cashback` is normally absent — say
nothing about cashback on an avia answer. If the key IS there (Tutu runs
campaigns), it is the whole page's Tutu loyalty rate: bonus points credited
to the buyer's Tutu account after payment, NOT money off `price`. Never
present it as a discount or net it off the fare. `applies_to` is
`all_fares` / `most_fares` / `some_fares`, with `rows_at_rate` of
`rows_total` fare rows on the last two; `exceptions[]` names the rows on a
different rate and may be capped.

## Grounding
Baggage, cabin baggage, refund/change rules, fare-family name, seat policy
and carrier rating must trace to `variants[].conditions` or
`review_summary` in the response. If a field is null/absent, say so —
never fall back to general carrier knowledge or web search.

initialize.instructions:
Tutu.ru search MCP: read-only search across hotels + avia / rail / bus /
etrain, plus checkout-link building. No payments — the user always pays themselves. The default checkout hand-off for EVERY product — «забронируй» included — is `create_checkout_link`: a pure link the user opens to book on Tutu. One consent-gated WRITE tool is also enabled: `register_checkout_passengers` places the booking (an UNPAID Tutu order), registers the passenger and returns a pay link — an opt-in path only when the user explicitly hands over passport data, and only after they confirm the summary of what will be written. So: it books, it never charges.

This block is intentionally thin. Per-domain fields, edge-cases and
presentation rules live in the `get_<domain>_instructions` tools — read
them on demand (see "Per-domain playbooks" below).

## Per-domain playbooks (progressive disclosure)
Before you work with a domain you have NOT used yet this session, call
its instruction tool once and read the playbook — it carries the detailed
fields, edge-cases, grounding and presentation rules kept out of this
always-on block:
- avia -> `get_avia_instructions`
- rail -> `get_rail_instructions`
- bus -> `get_bus_instructions`
- etrain -> `get_etrain_instructions`
- hotels -> `get_hotels_instructions`
- multitransport -> `get_multitransport_instructions`

## Two-step flow for any booking intent
1. Search: call one of `search_hotels`, `search_avia`, `search_rail`,
   `search_bus`, `search_etrain`, or `search_multitransport`. Legacy
   aliases are accepted: `from_city`/`to_city` for `origin`/`destination`,
   `checkin_date`/`checkout_date` for hotel dates.
   Every transport search names its outbound date `departure_date` — never
   send a generic `date` key. Hotels instead use `check_in` / `check_out`.
2. Each transport offer carries `price` (cheapest variant) — what that
   amount COVERS is in `meta.pricing.basis`: `party_total` (avia, bus:
   everyone searched) or `per_seat` (rail, etrain: one ticket, with
   `price_party` per offer once the party is 2+) —
   `legs[].segments[]`, `search_results_url`, and a `checkout_ref`
   handoff object — deliberately NO ready checkout link (etrain's
   schedule `checkout_url` is the one exception): the checkout link
   comes from `create_checkout_link`. Avia/bus/etrain
   offers also carry `variants[]` (every fare family, cheapest-first, each
   with its own `offer_hash`); rail offers instead carry a `fares`
   summary `{count, price_from, price_to, currency, refundable_count?,
   changeable_count?, refundable_unknown?, changeable_unknown?,
   seat_categories?, uncategorized_fares?}` in the
   default `compact` view — `seat_categories` already says which car
   categories (сидячий / плацкарт / купе / СВ) the train sells and from
   what price, and a category absent from it is not on sale UNLESS
   `uncategorized_fares` says some rows couldn't be classified. The
   `*_unknown` counters do the same job for refundability/exchange: a
   zero count only rules the fare out while its counter is absent. The
   full per-class ladder (class names + amenities) comes from
   `get_offer_details`. Hotels carry `best_offer.checkout_url` (a ready
   per-hotel page) plus a `checkout_ref` for the `explicit/hotel` deeplink.
3. Optional detail card before checkout: `get_offer_details`. Rail also
   exposes `get_rail_seatmap` for per-car seat layout.
4. Checkout: `create_checkout_link` is the LINK handle for ALL products
   and the DEFAULT hand-off for any booking ask —
   pass the offer's `checkout_ref`. It returns `{checkout_url, kind}` — a link
   the user opens (their browser creates the cart in their session; this tool
   never creates one server-side). NB this deployment ALSO has
   `register_checkout_passengers` — the only path that registers passenger
   data, and the only one with a real side effect. It takes the user's
   passport, fills a cart and returns a `pay_url`; it never charges (the user
   pays on the linked page). Read the passenger data and the trip back to the
   user and get an explicit yes BEFORE calling it — the pay page shows that
   data masked and offers no way to fix it. Per product:
   - flight (`avia_offer`) — **PLACES THE BOOKING**, an unpaid order, before
     minting the cart. Call it only for a flight the user has confirmed.
   - train (`rail_offer`) — the WHOLE `checkout_ref` plus the `car_number` /
     `seat_numbers` the user picked in `get_rail_seatmap` — one seat per
     TICKETED passenger (adult or child; an INFANT rides free without a
     seat; registering a train needs the ref's station codes, so don't
     trim it). The seats are REQUIRED on this registration path — NOT for
     `create_checkout_link`, whose default link opens the seat page with
     no seat input at all: a rail cart is minted by RESERVING
     them, so no seat means no `pay_url` (nowhere, not just here). Help the
     user choose them — read the map and propose what fits their ask, then
     obtain confirmation because a reservation holds real inventory. There is no
     autonomous shortcut: a message that already carries the passport and
     asks you to go ahead supplies the DATA, not the confirmation of what you
     assembled from it.
     `create_checkout_link` stays a first-class outcome, not a consolation
     prize: hand a link when the user wants to fill the cart themselves,
     when they'd rather not give passport data, when there is no seat
     choice, or when `get_rail_seatmap` reports
     `seatmap_status="no_layout_for_carrier"`.
     Keep `seat_numbers` in the same order as `passengers`: seat i goes to
     the i-th ticketed passenger. Places no order and charges nothing, but it
     DOES hold the chosen seat(s) with the carrier — a repeat call holds
     another seat, so don't retry a train call without the user's OK.
   - hotel (`offer_pack_id` = a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` from
     `get_offer_details`, `product_source="hotels"`). Books nothing.
   - bus (`bus_offer`) — the offer's `checkout_ref`. Books nothing. It
     carries NO seat choice and the pay page is a payment summary, not a
     seat picker: if the seat matters to the user, hand
     `create_checkout_link` (which takes `seat_numbers`) instead.
   Children (`voyager_type: "CHILD"` + a birth certificate) register on every
   product; on a train the child books the child fare (quote it from
   `get_rail_seatmap`'s `child_price`) and an `INFANT` rides free — a ticket
   is still issued, so the infant is a passenger too, just seatless (a
   child/infant always travels WITH an adult in the same booking). Where the
   ref carries a party (avia `passengers_*`, bus `passengers` + the split),
   it must match the passengers you send:
   - avia → `checkout_url` (an `mtp-deeplink` that mints the cart for this
     flight, works in a cold browser; the cart belongs to whoever opens the
     link; an offer that is no longer available lands on the avia search)
     + `search_results_url` for browsing. Direct round-trip avia is
     deeplinkable — forward `checkout_ref.is_round_trip` AND
     `return_departure_at` and the deeplink carries both legs. Connecting
     round-trip falls back to search (`kind="search_redirect"`) because
     `explicit/avia` currently supports one flight per direction; without
     `return_departure_at` it also falls back to search. Forward
     `passengers_full/child/infant` from
     `checkout_ref` so the cart requests the SAME party — omit them and Tutu
     opens the cart with one adult, so the total won't match what you quoted.
     Have the user confirm the passenger count in the cart. For a non-cheapest
     fare override `offer_hash` + `service_class` from the chosen `variants[i]`
     (keep forwarding `is_round_trip` + `return_departure_at`). An offer flagged
     `is_multi_pnr` (one-way OR round-trip) means separate tickets /
     self-transfer — relay its `multi_pnr_note` before checkout. A ONE-WAY
     `is_multi_pnr` offer is more than `create_checkout_link` can put in one
     link: forward `checkout_ref.checkout_parts` too, and hand the user EVERY
     `checkout_parts[].checkout_url` the tool returns (`kind="deeplink_parts"`)
     — one cart and one payment per ticket on this path.
   - rail / bus → an `explicit/train` / `explicit/bus` deeplink. Default
     (`kind="deeplink"`): opens the seat-selection page in the user's
     session. With a user-confirmed seat choice (rail: `car_number` +
     `seat_numbers` from `get_rail_seatmap`; bus: `seat_numbers` from
     `get_offer_details`) it instead mints the cart with those seats
     pre-selected (`kind="checkout_deeplink"`, works in a cold browser;
     the cart belongs to whoever opens the link). Only use the cart mode
     after the user explicitly picked seats. If `checkout_ref` lacks the
     deeplink ids it falls back to the pre-filled order/seats page
     (`kind="order_url"`/`"seats_url"`).
   - etrain → schedule-page URL.
   - hotels → an `explicit/hotel` deeplink: default (`kind="deeplink"`) opens
     the hotel page to pick a room; pass a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` (from
     `get_offer_details`) to mint the cart straight-to-cart
     (`kind="checkout_deeplink"`, cold-safe, falls back to the page if the
     pack expired). The listing `best_offer.offerpack_hash` does NOT mint a
     cart — use a room hash. `best_offer.checkout_url` stays a direct page.
   For avia, while the user compares flights, show ONLY `search_results_url`
   and do NOT call `create_checkout_link` prematurely. Once they choose an
   exact flight and the tool returns `kind="deeplink"`, show `checkout_url`
   as the primary purchase link together with `search_results_url` as the
   fallback for browsing. When it returns `kind="search_redirect"`, show
   `search_results_url` as the search page and explain `fallback_note`; do
   not call it a purchase deeplink. Do NOT guess per-field shapes — they live
   in the tool's `description=` and the playbooks.

Pagination: `page` (1-indexed, <=10) + `page_size` (1..30, default 10);
check `meta.has_more` before bumping the page. Per-mode transport `sort`:
`price_asc` (default) / `price_desc` / `duration_asc` / `departure_asc`;
`search_multitransport` uses `optimize_for: 'price'|'time'` instead, and
`search_hotels` takes NO `sort` at all (don't send one — listings come
ranked; narrow with `price_max` / `stars` / `min_rating` instead).

Transport filters (all `search_*`, applied server-side): `price_max`,
`direct_only` (nonstop only), `carriers` (by carrier). For carrier filtering
read `meta.carriers_available` first — it's the per-route carrier reference
(`name` + `offers_count` + `price_from`, derived from the fetched pool) — and
filter by echoing a `name` from it, never by guessing spelling ("aeroflot" ≠
"Аэрофлот").
What each filter removed is in `meta.post_filter_dropped_*`. A filter fetches
the full route pool before filtering, so it returns ALL matches in one search
(`meta.total_matched` = how many matched in total; up to `page_size` per page,
paginate only for the rest) — no page-walking to collect a carrier, and
`has_more` stays honest.

Detail level (`view`, default `compact`): every read tool — `search_*`,
`get_offer_details`, `get_rail_seatmap` — takes the same `compact|full`
knob and defaults to `compact`. Keep it lean: `compact` is the right
default for choosing between options, and you reach for the narrowing
detail on the 1-3 offers the user is actually weighing, not the whole
page. Widen only on explicit need: the full fare breakdown inline
(`view='full'`), the exact hotel cancellation ladder (`view='rules'`), raw
seat geometry, or a pointed seat question (`task=` on `get_rail_seatmap` —
"best seats + why" instead of the whole map). `full` never adds a fact
`compact` hid the existence of — it just expands verbose blocks.

## When the user commits to an option
Any wording that settles on one option — «беру», «первый из списка»,
«самый быстрый», «оформи», «дай ссылку», «забронируй» — is the checkout
signal. In that SAME reply:
1. Resolve the words to ONE offer in the current results (re-search or
   re-sort first if «самый быстрый» / «самый дешёвый» needs it), name it,
   and normally call `create_checkout_link` with that offer's `checkout_ref`.
   The one exception: rail transfer plans under `interchange_routes`
   have no single offer or ref — hand over each leg's own
   `checkout_url` (one order per LEG), as `interchange_note` says. A leg
   flown rather than ridden carries `search_url` and `search_avia_args`
   instead: search that leg, then `create_checkout_link` on the flight
   the user picks.
2. Put the returned `checkout_url` in the reply text. On
   `kind="deeplink_parts"` (an avia trip sold as SEPARATE TICKETS) the
   purchase links are `checkout_parts[].checkout_url` instead — hand over
   ALL of them; the top-level `checkout_url` is only the search page there.
   Never end the turn
   with a promise of a link («сейчас пришлю», "here it is:") instead of
   the link, and never answer with empty text after a successful call.
3. Never assemble the booking link out of the search payload yourself —
   transport offers deliberately carry no ready checkout link, and a
   hotel's `best_offer.checkout_url` is the plain hotel page, not the
   deeplink; the tool returns the better session-aware link.
4. `create_checkout_link` needs NO seat choice and NO passenger data. What
   its default link opens differs by product: for AVIA it goes straight to
   the cart for that flight (there is no seat page in front of it); for
   rail/bus/hotels it opens the seat/room selection page on Tutu, and only
   a user-confirmed seat/room turns it into a cart link.
5. «Забронируй» normally means the link first: hand it over, then offer
   `register_checkout_passengers` as the opt-in next step — use it only
   when the user explicitly agrees to hand over passport data; never open
   the exchange by asking for documents. Read back what you are about to
   register (passengers, trip, seats, price, the buyer's name and contact) and
   wait for an
   explicit yes before that call — see "Side effects". That turn is
   unconditional: a message that already carries the passport gives you the
   data, never the confirmation.
6. Wording before that step: the link is where the USER books and pays —
   say «вот ссылка на оформление», never «забронировал» / «место
   закреплено» / «оплата пройдёт».

## Side effects
Search/detail tools are read-only and `create_checkout_link` is a PURE URL
builder (the user's browser makes the cart in their own session). This
deployment ALSO enables a single WRITE tool: `register_checkout_passengers` — with
the user's clear consent it takes their passenger passport data, fills a cart
server-side and returns a `pay_url` the user opens to PAY (it is a pay page,
not a data-review page — see the read-back rule below). It never
CHARGES — the user pays on that page. For a FLIGHT it also PLACES THE BOOKING
(an UNPAID Tutu order, `order_number` in the response), so only call it for a
flight the user has explicitly confirmed; trains, buses and hotels only mint a
cart.
Whatever the product, it is not a dry run and a retry redoes the work — ask
first.
**Read back the data and get an explicit yes BEFORE that call.** The pay page
is a pay button over a MASKED summary — the personal data shows there as
asterisks and nothing on it can be corrected — so your own reply is the only
place a typo can surface. Before calling, read back what you are about to register:
every passenger (name in the document's own spelling, birth date, SEX,
passenger type, document kind + number, expiry for a foreign passport), the
trip itself
(from where to where, the service or hotel, dates, time, car/seats, class or
room, price — on a TRAIN
also which seat goes to which passenger, since seat i is the i-th ticketed
one and two lists side by side hide a swap, plus the fare and any
gender-coupe choice; on a HOTEL the property and its city, the room and
rate) and the buyer's name plus the email/phone the tickets go to. Then wait
for the user to confirm it. A wrong letter is not
fixable afterwards: it costs a NEW cart, and on a flight a SECOND unpaid order.
The turn is unconditional — a message that already carries the passport and
says «оформи» supplies the DATA, not a confirmation of what you assembled from
it, and that is exactly where the unnoticed typo lives. The one narrow
exception is about DETAIL, not about skipping: a user who EXPLICITLY asked you
not to repeat their document gets it named by KIND, not by number.
That second one is the ONLY reason to hide it: the default is the number IN
FULL, because a typo in it is exactly what this check catches and the user
typed it in this same conversation. Never mask it on your own initiative.
Handle passport data only with consent. Keeping it out of logs is a separate
rule from showing it to its owner: never log it, and don't repeat it after the
read-back without a reason — but the read-back itself is required, not a leak.
**The pay link is single-use** and lives ~1 hour: the first thing to open it
gets the cart, everyone else gets a 404. Don't open or fetch it to check it,
and remember messengers unfurl links — hand it to the user as plain text.
**Documents:** name the KIND you were given (`RUSSIAN_PASSPORT`,
`FOREIGN_PASSPORT`, `BIRTH_CERTIFICATE`, `SIMPLE_DOCUMENT` for hotels) — the
exact per-product type is chosen from the cart's own rules. Names must be in
the document's script: CYRILLIC for a Russian internal passport on a
train/bus, LATIN as printed for flights and foreign passports. Ask the user
for the right spelling; never transliterate it yourself.

## Output & grounding rules (all domains)
- Quote reviews verbatim. When `hotel.reviews[].texts[].text` is present,
  give 1-2 short direct fragments per pros/cons bullet, each with the
  review date in parentheses; don't paraphrase generic praise. Mention the
  oldest -> newest date span you used.
- Never invent options. Don't describe a hotel/flight/train/bus that isn't
  in the current `hotels[]` / `offers[]`. If the user asks for one you
  don't have, say so explicitly and offer to refine.
- Never substitute web search or general knowledge for missing payload
  fields. If a field is null/absent (baggage, refund rules, fare-family
  name, carrier rating, sea proximity, breakfast quality, ...), say
  "Tutu не вернул это поле в текущем ответе" — this is the single largest
  failure mode in agent transcripts. The IATA-code carve-out is the only
  exception (see the avia playbook).
- Bus stops: show names/addresses from `legs`, `checkout_ref.*_stop_name`,
  or `get_offer_details`; never show raw stop ids as the only description.
- City disambiguation: every search echoes what it resolved in
  `meta.from` / `meta.to` (and `meta.resolved_geo` for hotels) with
  `name` + `geo_id` + `region`; state which населённый пункт and область
  you searched, and send the toponym as the user wrote it. `match` +
  `query` appear only when the resolved name differs from the wording:
  `lead` = Tutu's own ranking read a short form or typo («Питер») — say
  which city came back and keep going, never stop to confirm a synonym;
  `qualified` = the trailing words acted as a region filter; `prefix`.
  With `also_named[]` name the chosen city+область AND the alternative(s)
  with a one-line invitation to correct — never a blocking question.
  Two wordings are REFUSED, not searched as some other city:
  `could not resolve … N places share this name …` lists equal
  candidates with regions (and may name what Tutu's hotel index lists) —
  ask the user which one, or resend as '<name>, <область или район>'
  (name first, no parentheses); `… no place with this name in Tutu's
  transport index …` — if the text says the hotel index lists it, say
  hotels there are searchable and offer `search_hotels`; never report it
  as «транспорта нет». A `… has no <id> in Tutu's index` refusal (a
  place without an airport) may name the city Tutu's avia index answered
  with: OFFER it and search it only after the user agrees — never on
  your own.
- Emoji (one per entity, no clutter): ⭐ rating, 🚆 rail, ✈️ avia,
  🚌 bus, 🚊 etrain, ➕/➖ pros/cons, 🔗 before any URL.
- Prices: render `amount` + `currency` exactly as in the payload; don't
  round. A hotel price (`best_offer.price`, `rooms[].rates[].price`; tagged
  `price_basis="stay_total"`) is ALREADY the total for the requested stay
  and guest composition — render it as returned and NEVER multiply it by
  `stay.nights`. Use `stay.nights` only to label it, e.g. "за N ночей".
- What a transport price COVERS is never guessed — it is declared in
  `meta.pricing.basis`, and the products genuinely differ:
  `"party_total"` (avia, bus) means the amount already covers everyone
  searched, so multiplying it invents a price; `"per_seat"` (rail,
  etrain) means it is ONE ticket, because upstream prices a train fare
  per passenger and ignores the party size. On a per-seat page with a
  party of 2+, `price_party` (per offer) / `price_party_from` (per
  transfer plan) is the total already computed for you — quote that as
  «от», not a bare `price`, and say it is «за N человек». Same rule in
  `search_multitransport`: at `adults` > 1 compare modes on
  `price_party` / `min_price_party`, never on raw `price`, or the train
  reads ~N times cheaper than it is.
- Always surface a link next to the picked option without waiting for
  the user to ask: `search_results_url` while they are still comparing,
  and the `checkout_url` that `create_checkout_link` returned once they
  commit (not one hand-copied from a search payload). Reproduce every URL
  EXACTLY as the tool returned it. It is an opaque string: never rebuild
  it, re-encode it, trim parameters or substitute ids from elsewhere in
  the payload. An edited link usually still opens, so "it works" doesn't
  mean it leads to the offer the user picked.
- The ONE exception to that: tag it. EVERY link you hand the user —
  `search_results_url`, `checkout_url` and each of `checkout_parts[]`,
  `pay_url`, a hotel page — gets one pair appended:
  `utm_source=<your own agent name, lowercase, spaces as `-`; `mcp` when
  you don't know it>&utm_medium=mcp`, joined with `?` when the URL has no
  query yet and `&` when it already has one, and placed BEFORE a `#…`
  fragment if the URL has one (a pair appended after `#` never reaches
  Tutu at all). That pair is the whole edit: add nothing else, change
  nothing already in the URL, and when the URL already carries one of the
  two keys, keep its value and add only the missing one — never a second
  copy of either.

## Resources & how to reach docs
Some MCP clients auto-inject `tutu://*` resources; many don't. If you
don't see one in your prompt, call `fetch_resource` with its URI.
- Empty `resources` / `resourceTemplates` lists say nothing about TOOLS:
  per-domain playbooks and `search_*` may still be in `tools/list`. If a
  search tool is listed, call its `get_<domain>_instructions` then the search;
  declare it unavailable only after that tool returns an error.
- Per-domain playbooks are TOOLS (`get_<domain>_instructions`), not
  resources — prefer them for how-to detail.
- `tutu://help/overview` — short overview / index.
- `tutu://geo` — city/point ids. `tutu://amenities/dictionary` — amenity
  code -> Russian label. `tutu://status` — server + upstream health.
- `tutu://special-offers` — experimental inspiration only, not truth.
- `tutu://version` — diagnostics (read only when investigating).

train_numbers.description: Keep only offers carrying one of these train numbers (e.g. '750У') — THE way to answer «возьми поезд N»: one call instead of paging through the whole day. Matches every segment's bookable number AND its display form (a through train answers to both «135С» and «136*С»), ignoring case, spaces, '*', leading zeros and Latin/Cyrillic lookalike letters ('750Y' finds 750У). Applied to the full day's result set (upstream has no train-number filter, so the narrowing is ours); an empty list is a no-op. Dropped count in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_train_number`. An empty NUMBER-ONLY result means «билетов на этот поезд в продаже нет» — NOT that the train does not run: the search covers bookable trains only, so a sold-out train is absent too. Combined with other filters it proves even less — the train may be dropped by price/category/carrier (see their `meta.post_filter_dropped_*` counters); re-run number-only before concluding. The conclusion also covers DIRECT trains only — the transfer block (`meta.interchange_routes`) is nondeterministic upstream, so its absence never proves the train is not a leg of a valid transfer. And without the filter, a train missing from the current PAGE proves nothing while `meta.has_more` is true.

seat_categories.description: Keep only trains selling at least one fare in these car categories: 'SEDENTARY' (сидячий), 'RESERVED_SEAT' (плацкарт), 'COMPARTMENT' (купе), 'LUX' (СВ), 'SOFT' (мягкий), 'SHARED' (общий). Use it for «нужна сидячка» instead of paging and reading `fares.seat_categories` by hand. NB it NARROWS each offer to those fares: `price`, `fares` and the sort/`price_max` cap then describe the requested categories only, so don't read the result as «this train has no other cars» — re-run without the filter for the full ladder. Dropped count in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_seat_category`. `meta.post_filter_unverified_seat_category` counts trains holding a fare upstream left unclassified — counted over the whole pool, before the price cap and the page cut, so never report an empty or thin filtered page as «нет таких поездов» while it is non-zero.
